_note: Gap-fill pass on the newly elected state legislative waves (November 2026). Every member of the six state legislative waves who held fewer than five stated positions and whose campaign issues or platform page still read was re-read on that same page (or, where the record's source is a platform index, one of its own sub-pages). Any further explicit, on-topic claim on an issue key already in the related-issues map was filed in politician-stances.js (regenerated into politician-stances-ext.js), appended after the member's existing cards and marked claim:'campaign'. Each line quotes the page. No roster row, board, issue key, related-issues pair, drawer code, route or gate changed, and there is no migration. Members whose page held nothing further are listed under unchanged with the reason, and their cards are byte-identical. Declared in scripts/v103-chrome-seams.mjs (DECLARED_STANCE_PASSES, newly_elected_state_legislative_gap_fill_nov2026). Read by scripts/test-newly-elected-state-legislative-gap-fill-2026.mjs and by each wave's own suite, which adds 'added' to the wave record's issueKeys.

added.text: Butler says "We need to make sure we continue to fund permanent supportive housing, homeless shelters, and mental health supports to tackle the rapidly growing problem of homelessness."
Butler backs higher rates on Coloradans earning over $500k to fund schools, roads and child care, saying those who can afford it should "pay a little more–to pay their fair share."
Livingston would end special breaks for big corporations and redirect that support to local businesses, pledging: "I'll fight to expand small-business funding."
Spotleson's issues page lists his video statement "Nevada can lead the world by example in Fighting Climate Change."
Spotleson's issues page lists his video statement "We need better Mental Health Accessibility," alongside "Mental Health Creates School Safety."

Leahy says "No one should ever have to choose between getting the medical care they need and putting food on the table" and will work to widen affordable coverage.
Leahy pledges "voting against any AI data center that tries to use resources from the Ogallala Aquifer, our public power, or pollutes our air."
Faulting a revenue system that taxes the very richest at the same rate as a family making $57,000, Leahy will work to "responsibly grow our revenues" and "prevent cuts to critical services."

Johnson "will work to increase access to high quality jobs and wages that keep up with the cost of living."

Wilcox backs more mental health resources "By strengthening prevention, improving access, and reducing stigma."
Wilcox would "Prioritize the maintenance and repair of critical infrastructure" so roads and bridges stay safe for residents, school buses and emergency vehicles.

Pereira pledges to "recruit and retain the best first responders by supporting good pay and retirement benefits" for police, firefighters and EMTs.
Pereira "will support apprenticeships and other career transition assistance for veterans returning to civilian life."
Pereira would "offer incentives to developers who build one-floor condos, townhomes, 55-plus communities, and mixed-income senior developments."
Under safe communities, Reinke lists "Supporting border security, local law enforcement, and strong public safety."
Swensen pledges: "I'll fight to support our small businesses, make housing affordable, and bring in good-paying jobs."
Swensen says "Families are already stretched thin" and pledges to "ease the cost of living."
Stravato's vision is "to roll back the red tape that constrains businesses from starting, growing, and staying in Rhode Island."
Horsted pledges to "Work toward accessible, affordable healthcare" so people can get the care they need without unnecessary financial barriers.
Tollefson says "No family should have to worry about getting sick or injured and not being able to afford proper medical care."
Delmay "will also work to lower healthcare bills through a transparent system that puts patients first."
Delmay will fight for "stormwater and drainage improvements, stronger infrastructure, and the resources communities need to prepare for extreme weather."
Lounsbury will "push back against the universal EdChoice school voucher system," saying public dollars should not finance private education.
